paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The average probing accuracy using different MLP variations. We indicate the size(s) of hidden layer(s) in square brackets.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the average probing accuracy difference between two multilingual BERT models, mBERT (light blue bars) and XLM-R (dark blue bars), across four different MLP (multilayer perceptron) configurations, with the vertical axis representing the percentage point difference in accuracy ranging from -0.2 to +0.2 in linear scale and the horizontal axis listing the MLP configurations: “hidden:[50], linear”, “hidden:[], linear”, “hidden:[100], ReLU”, and “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU”. For the “hidden:[50], linear” configuration, mBERT shows a negative difference of approximately -0.15 percentage points, while XLM-R shows a negative difference of approximately -0.05 percentage points. For the “hidden:[], linear” configuration, mBERT shows a positive difference of approximately +0.09 percentage points, while XLM-R shows a positive difference of approximately +0.21 percentage points. For the “hidden:[100], ReLU” configuration, mBERT shows a negative difference of approximately -0.12 percentage points, while XLM-R shows a positive difference of approximately +0.03 percentage points. For the “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU” configuration, mBERT shows a negative difference of approximately -0.18 percentage points, while XLM-R shows a negative difference of approximately -0.15 percentage points. The bars are grouped by configuration, with each group containing two bars side-by-side for the two models, and are not sorted by value.
